summary: The customer wants to explore an in situ optical spectroscopy pilot to monitor glucose and lactate in a cell culture process in order to detect changes faster than existing laboratory sampling allows.

facts_stated.text: The customer operates a cell culture process in an aqueous medium.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: We run a cell culture process in an aqueous medium.

facts_stated.text: Glucose and lactate are currently measured from discrete samples, causing delays in seeing changes.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: Glucose and lactate are measured from samples, and the delay makes it difficult to see changes promptly.

facts_stated.text: The culture medium and cell population change over the course of the run.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The medium and cell population change during the run

facts_stated.text: No probe or calibration strategy has been chosen yet.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: we have not yet selected a probe or a calibration strategy.

targets.purpose: monitoring cell culture changes promptly in situ
monitoring cell culture changes promptly in situ

process.value: prompt detection required because current sample measurement delay is problematic
process.enquiry_quote: the delay makes it difficult to see changes promptly

process.value: medium and cell population change during the run
process.enquiry_quote: The medium and cell population change during the run

customer_premises.claim: The in situ spectroscopy pilot can be directly cross-checked against and calibrated by existing laboratory sample measurements without accounting for sampling delays or differences.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: can be checked against those existing laboratory measurements

unknowns: Concentration ranges and detection limits for glucose and lactate
